details.publicNotes:
Vernals are the tempestuous, fickle maestros of the four seasonal fey. Riding the storm winds and volatile weather fronts common in spring, vernals embody nature's potential for sudden and chaotic change, whether whimsical or tempestuous. Unlike other seasonals, vernals don't share the spotlight gladly with others of their own kind; when vernals happen to meet on the capricious winds of a storm, they engage in deafening sonic sky-duels to claim "ownership" rights over the spring squall. Vernals are quick to respond to challenges to their authority over the storms with a little bit of intimidation or violence, yet they just as quickly grow bored of opponents who lack the determination and skill to keep up with them. An attacking vernal's goal is to display their dominance and leave their opponent cowed and in awe, or at least to enjoy an exciting bout with a worthy adversary, rather than to annihilate an unworthy foe who wastes their thunder.

A vernal's music can seem discordant and cacophonous to the untrained ear, but remarkable artistry hides within the walls of sound torn loose from their crackling instruments. It is said that a vernal never plays the same song twice, always improvising and duetting with the lightning, thunder, hail-clatter, and sleet-noise of their accompanying storms. Humanoids of various ancestries have claimed the violent clash of a vernal's music resonates and gives voice to their own turbulent emotions, and some of these "stormchasers" rush to follow a vernal's tempest as it tours across the land and sea, in a dangerous attempt to find themselves.

Seasonals are a cycle of four kinds of fey, each tied to one of the four seasons: vernals who embody spring's renewal and storming showers, aestivals who embody summer's lazy heat and burning passion, autumnals who embody the melancholy culling and reaping harvest of autumn, and hibernals who embody winter's quiet cheer.

Whatever the current season in the mortal world, seasonals wrap themselves in a metaphysical cloak of their own season's magic and carry the songs full of that season's surging emotions with them wherever they go in the mortal world or across the realm of Faerie. Whenever seasonals meet, shy hibernals typically prefer to amuse themselves by watching the antics of the other three kinds of fey, while vernals impatiently call for energetic contests, aestivals languidly nap until roused to fiery bursts of activity, and autumnals attempt to imbue a sense of stark responsibility in the rest of their compatriots. Exceptions exist, with those seasonals interacting with the others in ways unexpected based upon the stereotypes of their season.

Storm Songs

Vernals consider themselves the premier conductors of the elements, and meetings between them and other atmospheric musicians are sure to strike sparks. They have a particular rivalry with storm conductors. When the two meet, their twin cloud formations often remain fixed in place over some unfortunate locale, unleashing increasingly violent storms as the spirits engage in a battle for supremacy.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 45/100/180 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning), perception item, skill items (Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Intimidation, Nature, Performance, Stealth)

A bolt of lightning strikes outward from your hand, dealing 4d12 electricity damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12.

A cacophonous noise blasts out, dealing 2d10 sonic damage. Each creature must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage.

Failure The creature takes full damage and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round.

Critical Failure The creature takes double damage, is deafened for 1 minute, and is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.dfCMdR4wnpbYNTix]{Stunned 1}.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10.

You call down a tendril of lightning that cracks with thunder, dealing 1d12 electricity damage and 1d4 sonic damage to the target with a basic Reflex save. A target wearing metal armor or made of metal takes a –1 circumstance bonus to its save, and if damaged by the spell is @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for 1 round.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12 electricity and 1d4 sonic.

A bolt of lightning strikes outward from your hand, dealing 4d12 electricity damage.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d12.

A high-frequency sonic attack shatters a nearby object. You deal 2d10 sonic damage to the object, ignoring the object's Hardness if it is 4 or lower.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d10, and the Hardness the spell ignores increases by 2.

You create a barrier of gusting winds that hinders anything moving through it. The wall of swirling winds is 5 feet thick, 60 feet long, and 30 feet high. The wall stands vertically, but you can shape its path. Though the wall of wind distorts the air, it does not hamper sight. The wall has the following effects.

  • Ammunition from physical ranged attacks-such as arrows, bolts, sling bullets, and other objects of similar size-can't pass through the wall. Attacks with bigger ranged weapons, such as javelins, take a -2 circumstance penalty to their attack rolls if their paths pass through the wall. Massive ranged weapons and spell effects that don't create physical objects pass through the wall with no penalty.
  • The wall is difficult terrain to creatures attempting to move overland through it. Gases, including creatures in @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.V8wXOsoejQhe6CyG]{Vapor Form}, can't pass through the wall.
  • A creature that attempts to fly through the wall using a move action must attempt a Fortitude save.

Critical Success The creature can move through the wall normally this turn.

Success The flying creature can move through the wall this turn, but the wall is difficult terrain.

Failure The wall stops the movement of the flying creature, and any remaining movement from its current action is wasted.

Critical Failure As failure, and the creature is pushed 10 feet away from the wall.

An arc of lightning leaps from one target to another. Each target takes 2d4 electricity damage with a basic Reflex save.

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

In your mind's eye, you magically reorient yourself. You immediately know which direction is north (if it exists at your current location), and you can choose a location you were at within the last 24 hours and learn what direction it lies.

Heightened (3rd) You can choose a location you were at within the last week.

Heightened (7th) You can choose a location you were at regardless of how long ago you were there.

You stir up the air around you to propel yourself toward a foe, then slice into them with blades of air. Stride up to half your Speed toward a target, then make a melee spell attack roll against the target's AC. If you hit, the target takes 2d4 slashing damage (double damage on a critical hit).

Heightened (+1) The damage increases by 1d4.

Attempts to hinder the vernal's passage are met with a punishing crack of thunder. A creature that successfully Strikes the vernal with a reaction triggered by movement takes @Damage[4d6[sonic]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:25|basic] save). On a failure, they are also @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.conditions.Item.9PR9y0bi4JPKnHPR]{Deafened} for 1 round.

Trigger A creature within 60 feet uses an ability with the auditory or sonic traits

Effect With overwhelming sound, the vernal attempts to counteract the effect, with a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+17 #Counteract]]{+17} and a counteract rank of 4.

Requirements The vernal is adjacent to at least one enemy

Effect Letting loose a sonic boom, the vernal Strides or Flies twice to a space not adjacent to any enemies. All enemies adjacent to the vernal at any point take @Damage[6d6[sonic]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:25] save). Any creature that fails its save is pushed back 5 feet from the movement path (or 10 feet on a critical failure). The vernal can't use Thunderous Retreat again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Thunderous Retreat]]{1d4 rounds}.

A vernal can cast their @UUID[Compendium.sf2e.spells.Item.kBhaPuzLUSwS6vVf] cantrip with a single action to target only one creature, or they can instead use three actions to target three creatures and increase the damage dice to d6s.
